approaches_tried.description: Plan's literal COMMAND_SCAN construction using the `:a;N;$!ba` slurp-mode sed idiom, implemented verbatim
approaches_tried.reason: GNU sed's N command, invoked when the current line is already the last line of input (true of any single-line command, i.e. most commands), finds no next line to append, auto-prints the pattern space UNMODIFIED, and terminates the script before the substitution ever runs. Verified by direct reproduction: `printf 'git commit -m "fix -a bug"' | sed -e ':a' -e 'N' -e '$!ba' -e 's/"[^"]*"/""/g'` returns the input completely unstripped. This regressed the baseline: git commit -m mentions -a in quotes (single-line) case (previously GREEN pre-fix, went RED under this construction). Replaced with `sed -z` (NUL-delimited records), which treats the whole command -- single- or multi-line alike -- as one record with no last-line special case; re-verified 43/43 green after the substitution.
